subject: Post-demo: deployment preference check-in and hosted quickstart options (Nozzle Labs)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@nozzlelabs.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — runtime fit and deployment options

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can recommend the right onramp: 

Summary:
- Demo focus: conversational summarization + search re-ranking for support tickets.
- Nozzle's priority: low median latency (<200ms p50 for single-turn responses) and strong data isolation for PII.

Clarifying questions to help us recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC:
1) Do you need a VPC/network peering connection (customer-managed) for all traffic, or would you accept TLS-only traffic to our hosted endpoints?
2) Expected steady-state QPS and target concurrency (avg requests/sec and peak burst in requests/min)?
3) Any regulatory requirement for on-prem / air-gapped processing (HIPAA, CCPA/CCPA-Specific retention rules)?

If Hosted API looks viable we can spin up a sandbox with a prefetched KV cache strategy and propose endpoint mappings and rate limits for a 2-week pilot. I attached a short checklist that explains the quickstart steps and what we typically allocate in hosted trials.

Next step suggestion: if you can send the answers above, Diego and I will prepare a short mutual action plan and a recommended ratecap + endpoint matrix for the sandbox. Would Tuesday morning PST work for a 15-min alignment?

Thanks —
Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Alex Turner <alex@nozzlelabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — runtime fit and deployment options

Grace — great demo, thanks. Quick answers below; Priya is looped for security/regulatory confirmation.

1) VPC: preferred but not strictly required for the pilot. For production we will likely require VPC peering for customer data flows. Pilot can be TLS-only to simplify onboarding.
2) Traffic: steady ~8 QPS for the initial pilot (9-5 support load), with bursts up to ~60 reqs/min during release windows. Typical request payloads are 1.5–2k tokens.
3) Regulations: Nozzle handles EU customers and has data residency needs (EU), but US-based pilot ok. No formal HIPAA requirement today.

Also: we want to understand your hosted rate limiting model — do you rate-limit by API key, by endpoint, or by model? What's the typical burst strategy?

We can do Tuesday 9:30am PST for a quick alignment.

—Alex
Head of Engineering, Nozzle Labs
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@nozzlelabs.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — runtime fit and deployment options

Thanks Alex — helpful. Short answers to the rate-limit question and pilot proposal: 

Rate limiting model (hosted):
- Primary: per-API-key soft-windowed quotas (tokens/sec and requests/sec) with token-based metering (you see per-token cost).
- Secondary: per-endpoint concurrency ceilings to protect latency SLOs (we surface p50/p95/P99 per route in Console).
- Burst strategy: short token bursts are allowed up to a configured burst window; sustained bursts will be throttled and we recommend a burst reserve capacity for launches.

Pilot proposal (Hosted sandbox):
- Provision a hosted sandbox API key scoped to Nozzle's pilot.
- Endpoint mapping: one chat endpoint for the summarizer (prefetch + KV cache), one inference endpoint for reranking.
- Suggested ratebands for pilot: 10 QPS steady, 65 reqs/min burst cap, token ceiling 250K tokens/min.
- EU data residency: we can route pilot traffic through our eu-west region for data residency testing; note Hosted still requires contractual addendum for residency SLA.

I'll attach a mutual action plan template — Grace and I can prefill with the pilot cadence and measurables (latency targets, quality checks). Alex — for the VPC requirement, since production will likely want peering, we'll include dedicated capacity as an explicit option in the MAP and list preflight gating criteria.

Next steps:
- Grace: will send the filled checklist + a draft MAP before our 9:30am call.
- Alex: please confirm the EU pilot scope (do you want EU-only test traffic?).

Regards,
Diego
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-nozzle-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — runtime fit and deployment options

Great — thanks Alex + Diego. Quick confirmations ahead of the 9:30am PST alignment:

1) We'll provision a hosted sandbox API key scoped to Nozzle and route test traffic to eu-west if you confirm EU scope. For the pilot we'll accept TLS-only connectivity; we will include VPC peering as an explicit production requirement in the MAP.
2) Pilot ratebands (we'll prefill but can tune): steady 10 QPS, burst 65 reqs/min, token ceiling 250K/min.
3) Deliverables before the call: prefilled quickstart checklist (attached), draft MAP with gating criteria and fallback to Dedicated if VPC peering is required sooner.

Agenda for 9:30 (15m):
- Confirm EU pilot scope and connectivity for sandbox (5m)
- Agree pilot ratebands and success criteria (latency p50 <200ms, p95 <600ms) (7m)
- Next steps: sign trial addendum and provision API key (3m)

If anything else to add to the agenda, flag it now. Otherwise see you at 9:30.

Thanks —
Grace
